--- title: "olsrr 0.7.1" author: "Aravind Hebbali" date: "2026-11-19" description: "What is new in olsrr since 2019: locked predictors in stepwise selection, model comparison, weighted regression summaries, and calculation fixes across diagnostics and tests." image: "/img/olsrr-0-7-1.png" image-alt: "olsrr hex logo next to the tagline Tools for building and checking OLS regression models in R, the line 0.7.1, corrected test results, the package name olsrr and olsrr.rsquaredacademy.com" categories: ["packages", "regression"] tags: ["olsrr"] execute: freeze: true include-in-header: text: | --- ![](/img/olsrr-0-7-1.png){fig-alt="olsrr hex logo next to the tagline Tools for building and checking OLS regression models in R, the line 0.7.1, corrected test results, the package name olsrr and olsrr.rsquaredacademy.com" width="100%"} ```{=html} ``` `olsrr` 0.7.1 is on CRAN. `olsrr` provides tools for building and checking ordinary least squares regression models in R: regression summaries, variable selection, heteroskedasticity and normality tests, collinearity diagnostics, influence measures and residual plots, all built around `lm()` objects. We don't usually write about patch releases, but this one deserves a post: - Several test and summary results change: Holm-adjusted Breusch-Pagan $p$-values, the Cramér–von Mises normality test, and the residual MSE/RMSE in model summaries. If you report these numbers, please re-run your analyses. - Every calculation and plot was checked against base R and reference packages (`car`, `lmtest` and `nortest`) for this release. - It is the first `olsrr` post since our [introduction in 2019](../introducing-olsrr/index.qmd), so it also covers what has been added since then. **Who should read what:** if you report Holm-adjusted Breusch-Pagan $p$-values, Cramér–von Mises normality tests or MSE/RMSE from `olsrr`, read [Behaviour changes](#behaviour-changes) first. Everyone else can skip to [What's new since 2019](#whats-new-since-2019). You can install it from CRAN with: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} install.packages("olsrr") ``` ::: You can see a full list of changes in the [release notes](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/releases/tag/v0.7.1). ## Behaviour changes These fixes change numbers you may already have in reports. In each case 0.7.1 now agrees with the base R or reference implementation, so the new values are the ones to use. ::: {.ba-note} How we checked: every number in this post was re-run on CRAN `olsrr` 0.7.0 and 0.7.1, and the release passed an independent audit against base R, `car`, `lmtest` and `nortest` before it was submitted. ::: ### Breusch-Pagan test: Holm-adjusted p-values With `ols_test_breusch_pagan(..., rhs = TRUE, multiple = TRUE, p.adj = "holm")`, version 0.7.0 sorted the raw $p$-values and multiplied them by reversed ranks without the cumulative-maximum step of Holm's procedure. A predictor could keep an adjusted $p$-value that was too small and be wrongly flagged at $lpha = 0.05$. Version 0.7.1 uses `stats::p.adjust(p, "holm")`. In this three-predictor example the raw $p$-values are `0.0465`, `1.07e-05` and `0.0410`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(15) n <- 60 z <- rnorm(n) d <- data.frame(x1 = z + rnorm(n), x2 = z + rnorm(n), x3 = z + rnorm(n)) d$y <- rnorm(n) * exp(0.55 * z) m_bp <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = d) ols_test_breusch_pagan(m_bp, rhs = TRUE, multiple = TRUE, p.adj = "holm") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Breusch Pagan Test for Heteroskedasticity ----------------------------------------- Ho: the variance is constant Ha: the variance is not constant Data ------------------- Response : y Variables: x1 x2 x3 Test Summary (Holm's p values) ------------------------------------------------- Variable chi2 df p ------------------------------------------------- x1 3.962893 1 8.192284e-02 x2 19.381555 1 3.211077e-05 x3 4.177610 1 8.192284e-02 ------------------------------------------------- simultaneous 21.479644 3 8.369002e-05 ------------------------------------------------- ``` ::: ::: ```{=html}
olsrr 0.7.0
x10.0465
x23.21e-05
x30.0819
olsrr 0.7.1
x10.0819
x23.21e-05
x30.0819

Same call on both CRAN versions: ols_test_breusch_pagan(m_bp, rhs = TRUE, multiple = TRUE, p.adj = "holm"). Changed values are highlighted.

```
Code that produced both values ```r # Run once with each version, e.g. in two sessions: # remotes::install_version("olsrr", "0.7.0") # then # install.packages("olsrr") # 0.7.1 library(olsrr) set.seed(15) n <- 60 z <- rnorm(n) d <- data.frame(x1 = z + rnorm(n), x2 = z + rnorm(n), x3 = z + rnorm(n)) d$y <- rnorm(n) * exp(0.55 * z) m_bp <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = d) ols_test_breusch_pagan(m_bp, rhs = TRUE, multiple = TRUE, p.adj = "holm")$p ```
In 0.7.0, `x1` remained below `0.05` (`0.0465`) even though `x3` had a smaller raw $p$-value and adjusted to `0.0819`. In 0.7.1, `x1` is `0.0819`, matching `stats::p.adjust()`. **What to do:** re-run any Holm-adjusted Breusch-Pagan tests; the 0.7.1 values match `stats::p.adjust()`. ### Normality test: Cramér–von Mises In 0.7.0, `ols_test_normality()` compared the Cramér–von Mises statistic with a standard uniform distribution instead of a normal distribution with mean and standard deviation estimated from the residuals, so it rejected normality for almost any regression. Version 0.7.1 calls `nortest::cvm.test()`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + wt + qsec, data = mtcars) ols_test_normality(model) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ----------------------------------------------- Test Statistic pvalue ----------------------------------------------- Shapiro-Wilk 0.9366 0.0600 Kolmogorov-Smirnov 0.1152 0.7464 Cramer-von Mises 0.0764 0.2230 Anderson-Darling 0.5859 0.1188 ----------------------------------------------- ``` ::: ::: ```{=html}
olsrr 0.7.0
Cramér–von Mises W2.8122
p-value0.0000
olsrr 0.7.1
Cramér–von Mises W0.0764
p-value0.2230

Same call on both CRAN versions: ols_test_normality(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + wt + qsec, mtcars)). Changed values are highlighted.

```
Code that produced both values ```r # Run once with each version, e.g. in two sessions: # remotes::install_version("olsrr", "0.7.0") # then # install.packages("olsrr") # 0.7.1 library(olsrr) model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + wt + qsec, data = mtcars) ols_test_normality(model)$cramer ```
In 0.7.1, the Cramér–von Mises result (`p = 0.2230`) agrees with `nortest::cvm.test(residuals(model))` and aligns qualitatively with the Shapiro-Wilk (`0.0600`) and Anderson-Darling (`0.1188`) tests on the same residuals. (See [What's next](#whats-next) about the Kolmogorov-Smirnov row.) **What to do:** treat earlier Cramér–von Mises rejections from `olsrr` as unreliable and re-run the test. ### Residual MSE and RMSE In 0.7.0, `ols_regress()` and `ols_model_performance()` divided the residual sum of squares by $n$ rather than by the residual degrees of freedom ([#221](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/221), reported by [@viqule11](https://github.com/viqule11)). For `lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + wt + qsec, data = mtcars)` ($n = 32$, 27 residual degrees of freedom) that gave `MSE = 5.8011` and `RMSE = 2.4085`. Version 0.7.1 reports `MSE = 6.8754` and `RMSE = 2.6221`, matching the ANOVA residual mean square and `summary(model)$sigma`. ```{=html}
olsrr 0.7.0
MSE5.8011
RMSE2.4085
olsrr 0.7.1
MSE6.8754
RMSE2.6221

Same call on both CRAN versions: ols_regress(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + wt + qsec, mtcars)). Changed values are highlighted.

```
Code that produced both values ```r # Run once with each version, e.g. in two sessions: # remotes::install_version("olsrr", "0.7.0") # then # install.packages("olsrr") # 0.7.1 library(olsrr) model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + wt + qsec, data = mtcars) r <- ols_regress(model) c(mse = r$mse, rmse = r$rmse) ```
**What to do:** expect slightly larger MSE and RMSE values; they now match base R. ## What's new since 2019 ### Stepwise Selection with Locked Predictors Between versions 0.6.0 and 0.7.1, the variable selection family expanded to cover $p$-values, AIC, SBC (BIC), Sawa's BIC (`sbic`), $R^2$, and adjusted $R^2$. All forward, backward, and both-direction selectors now accept `include` and `exclude` arguments (by name or column index) so baseline covariates or confounders stay in the model throughout selection. On the `surgical` dataset, locking `age` and `alc_heavy` via `include` keeps both predictors in the base model (Step 0, `AIC = 795.956`) and through every subsequent addition and removal step, even though `age` itself has $p = 0.473$ in the final fit: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_surg <- lm( y ~ bcs + pindex + enzyme_test + liver_test + age + gender + alc_mod + alc_heavy, data = surgical ) ols_step_both_aic(m_surg, include = c("age", "alc_heavy")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Stepwise Summary ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Step Variable AIC SBC SBIC R2 Adj. R-Squared 0.750 Coef. Error Std. Beta t Sig lower upper ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ (Intercept) -1237.653 225.517 -5.488 0.000 -1691.085 -784.221 age -1.787 2.473 -0.050 -0.723 0.473 -6.759 3.184 alc_heavy 306.655 73.188 0.303 4.190 0.000 159.500 453.809 enzyme_test 11.244 1.314 0.601 8.555 0.000 8.601 13.887 pindex 10.062 1.633 0.428 6.163 0.000 6.779 13.344 bcs 81.587 17.870 0.329 4.566 0.000 45.657 117.516 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ``` ::: ::: ### Ten-Panel Diagnostic Grid `ols_plot_diagnostics()` gathers ten residual, fit, leverage, and influence views for an `lm` object: residuals vs fitted values, deleted studentized residuals vs predicted values, studentized residuals vs leverage, normal Q-Q plot, actual vs fitted values, Cook's D chart, centered fit spread, residual spread, residual histogram, and residual box plot. Calling `ols_plot_diagnostics(model)` directly pages the panels in 2×2 grids (and in 0.7.1 draws cleanly inside scripts, functions, and loops as well as at the top level). Setting `print_plot = FALSE` returns the ten `ggplot` objects without drawing them first, so they can be arranged in a single layout: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + wt + qsec, data = mtcars) panels <- ols_plot_diagnostics(model, print_plot = FALSE) gridExtra::grid.arrange(grobs = panels, ncol = 2, top = "Regression Diagnostics") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/diag-grid-1.png){fig-alt='Ten-panel regression diagnostic grid for mpg ~ disp + hp + wt + qsec on mtcars, arranged in five rows of two panels: Residual vs Fitted Values, Deleted Studentized Residual vs Predicted Values, Outlier and Leverage Diagnostics, Normal Q-Q Plot, Actual vs Fitted for mpg, Cook\'s D Chart, centered fit spread and residual spread plots, Residual Histogram with normal curve, and Residual Box Plot.' width=864} ::: ::: ### Model Performance and Multi-Model Comparison Added in 0.7.0 and refined in 0.7.1, `ols_model_performance()` reports fit metrics for a single model, while `ols_compare_model_performance()` places competing models side by side across $R^2$, adjusted $R^2$, predicted $R^2$, AIC, SBC, SBIC, RMSE, and residual standard error (`sigma`): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m1 <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars) m2 <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp + qsec, data = mtcars) m3 <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp + qsec + disp, data = mtcars) ols_compare_model_performance(m1, m2, m3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` name r2 r2_adj r2_pred aic sbc sbic rmse 1 m1 0.8267855 0.8148396 0.7810871 156.6523 162.5153 66.43956 2.593412 2 m2 0.8347678 0.8170643 0.7819955 157.1426 164.4713 67.43259 2.577785 3 m3 0.8351443 0.8107212 0.7710297 159.0696 167.8640 70.04081 2.622095 sigma 1 2.593412 2 2.577785 3 2.622095 ``` ::: ::: ### Weighted Linear Regression in `ols_regress()` In 0.7.1, `ols_regress()` supports weighted linear models fitted with `lm(..., weights = ...)`, matching base R's `summary()`, `anova()`, and `confint()` for coefficient estimates, standard errors, $t$-statistics, confidence intervals, $R^2$, residual standard error, the ANOVA table, standardized betas, and weighted predicted $R^2$: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} d_wt <- mtcars d_wt$w <- seq_len(nrow(d_wt)) / 8 m_w1 <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = d_wt, weights = w) ols_regress(m_w1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Model Summary --------------------------------------------------------------- R 0.917 RMSE 3.876 R-Squared 0.841 MSE 15.027 Adj. R-Squared 0.830 Coef. Var 19.295 Pred R-Squared 0.786 AIC 167.360 MAE 1.953 SBC 173.223 --------------------------------------------------------------- RMSE: Root Mean Square Error MSE: Mean Square Error MAE: Mean Absolute Error AIC: Akaike Information Criteria SBC: Schwarz Bayesian Criteria ANOVA -------------------------------------------------------------------- Sum of Squares DF Mean Square F Sig. -------------------------------------------------------------------- Regression 2308.267 2 1154.134 76.806 0.0000 Residual 435.769 29 15.027 Total 2744.036 31 -------------------------------------------------------------------- Parameter Estimates ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- model Beta Std. Error Std. Beta t Sig lower upper ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- (Intercept) 37.938 1.545 24.560 0.000 34.779 41.098 wt -4.102 0.613 -0.666 -6.691 0.000 -5.355 -2.848 hp -0.030 0.008 -0.345 -3.678 0.001 -0.047 -0.013 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ``` ::: ::: ## Other improvements - `ols_press()` weights the squared deleted residuals for weighted models, so `ols_pred_rsq()` no longer moves towards 1 when the weights are rescaled. For the weighted model shown above, multiplying the weights by 10 changed predicted $R^2$ from `0.9077` to `0.9908` in 0.7.0; in 0.7.1 both are `0.7859`. - `ols_plot_resid_hist()` draws the bars with the same breaks as the normal curve. Previously the curve could be drawn at about half its correct height (`0.54` of the expected peak for `lm(hwy ~ displ + cty + year, data = ggplot2::mpg)`). - `ols_plot_comp_plus_resid()` keeps every predictor for single-predictor and no-intercept models; 0.7.0 dropped a column and plotted a single point. - `ols_test_outlier()` caps Bonferroni-adjusted $p$-values at 1 (0.7.0 could report values such as `6.62`). - Information criteria count parameters with the model rank, which fixes factor predictors and rank-deficient models; `ols_aic(corrected = TRUE)` matches the AICc formula ([#224](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/224), [#170](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/170), reported by [@comatrion](https://github.com/comatrion)), and Mallows' $C_p$ is correct for factor predictors ([#92](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/92), reported by [@cccfran](https://github.com/cccfran)) and in `ols_step_all_possible()` ([#215](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/215), reported by [@LSantanaZA](https://github.com/LSantanaZA)). - Stepwise selection handles transformed and factor predictors in refits ([#244](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/244), [#246](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/246)), forward selection on saturated models ([#199](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/199), reported by [@hirscht](https://github.com/hirscht)), ties ([#206](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/206), reported by [@kaygmz](https://github.com/kaygmz)) and aliased terms ([#172](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/172), reported by [@yayyb](https://github.com/yayyb)). - Models fitted with `na.action = na.exclude` or with weights are handled consistently across plots and tests; diagnostics whose formulas assume unweighted least squares now stop with a clear error for weighted fits ([#236](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/236)). ## What's next Two issues remain open and will be fixed in 0.7.2. The Kolmogorov-Smirnov row of `ols_test_normality()` is not Lilliefors-corrected, so its $p$-value is too large when the mean and standard deviation are estimated from the residuals ([#254](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/254)). Until then, use the Shapiro-Wilk, Cramér–von Mises or Anderson-Darling rows, or call `nortest::lillie.test(residuals(model))`. Two panels of `ols_plot_diagnostics()` also share the title "Residual Fit Spread Plot" ([#253](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues/253)); the plotted values and axis labels are correct. ## Acknowledgements A big thank you to everyone who contributed to `olsrr` since 2019 by opening issues, reporting bugs and sending pull requests: [@AminHP](https://github.com/AminHP), [@aravindhebbali](https://github.com/aravindhebbali), [@ashimkapoor](https://github.com/ashimkapoor), [@bappa10085](https://github.com/bappa10085), [@ButlerMSDA](https://github.com/ButlerMSDA), [@CarlosJara72](https://github.com/CarlosJara72), [@comatrion](https://github.com/comatrion), [@davidreilly007](https://github.com/davidreilly007), [@DrMondesire](https://github.com/DrMondesire), [@grantbrown](https://github.com/grantbrown), [@hirscht](https://github.com/hirscht), [@hkincaid](https://github.com/hkincaid), [@iankelk](https://github.com/iankelk), [@jmberros](https://github.com/jmberros), [@jorgevallejo](https://github.com/jorgevallejo), [@jst04004](https://github.com/jst04004), [@jtheog](https://github.com/jtheog), [@kaygmz](https://github.com/kaygmz), [@linusjf](https://github.com/linusjf), [@LSantanaZA](https://github.com/LSantanaZA), [@modche](https://github.com/modche), [@Molina-Valero](https://github.com/Molina-Valero), [@mwm-cbus](https://github.com/mwm-cbus), [@njrockwood](https://github.com/njrockwood), [@paleolimbot](https://github.com/paleolimbot), [@PsychlytxTD](https://github.com/PsychlytxTD), [@qwertytam](https://github.com/qwertytam), [@sblanco74](https://github.com/sblanco74), [@sckott](https://github.com/sckott), [@SunsetBlvd](https://github.com/SunsetBlvd), [@tikuma-lsuhsc](https://github.com/tikuma-lsuhsc), [@vasili111](https://github.com/vasili111), [@viqule11](https://github.com/viqule11), [@williamlai2](https://github.com/williamlai2), and [@yayyb](https://github.com/yayyb).
